summary: Rules Desk for several customer organisations, plus structured request intake, grouped failed lookups and an AI lane that drafts routing rules for a lead to finish, inside limits enforced in code.

archetype.reason: A help desk product, not a platform for building others.

multi_tenant.reason: Several customer organisations, each with its own leads, agents and data.

hosted_service.reason: A web service and a drafting worker.

machine_actions.reason: A token-authenticated JSON API changes answers, rules, settings and drafts.

agent_mutations.reason: The AI writes drafts stored awaiting approval, which count as agent mutations.

evolution_auto_apply.reason: A draft goes live only when a lead publishes it.

definition_change_path.reason: Answers and rules are versioned definitions changed at runtime.

code_release_path.reason: The AI writes routing rules, which are declarative data, not code.

ai_features.reason: The drafting worker calls a language model.

ai_data_access.reason: The model receives failed questions and request text from the product's data.

DEL-01.reason: Requests are captured in the product with area, requester, examples and the rules involved; no specification or risk class.

DEL-04.reason: An AI lane drafts routing rules on request; a lead finishes and publishes them.

DEL-05.reason: CI on every pull request and checks on every answer, rule and AI draft; settings changes are unchecked.

ARC-01.reason: Relational queries with hand-made indexes; no search index.

ARC-02.reason: Numbered forward-only migrations applied by a command; no down steps. At 1 it keeps every architecture criterion at 1 or more for Level 2.

ARC-03.reason: Web instances are stateless with a documented caveat (one worker); scale-out is not exercised by tests or manifests.

ARC-04.reason: A jobs table with row locks and up to three attempts; no back-off between jobs, idempotency or dead-letter view.

ARC-05.reason: Data isolation is tested and per-organisation quotas exist, but there is no noisy-neighbour detection, so not 3.

ARC-06.reason: The only limit was found in an incident.

ARC-08.reason: Model calls have timeouts and retries and answering does not depend on the model; other surfaces have no isolation.

ARC-09.reason: A pg_dump backup command; the test only checks pg_dump is called, and restore is manual and never rehearsed.

LRN-03.reason: Failed lookups recorded with area, channel and rules version, queryable.

LRN-05.reason: Failed lookups grouped with samples, areas and the rules versions in force; no reproducible case or likely cause.

LRN-06.reason: Drafts for one area (routing rules) from a failure group or request; not ranked across the product.

LRN-07.reason: Experience is captured and candidate rules are generated when a lead asks, not continuously.

LRN-08.reason: AI drafts pass the same automated checks before a lead can publish; no evaluation against a baseline.

LRN-10.reason: Checks and the prompt are files changed only by engineers.

GOV-05.reason: History and undo for answers and rules; settings have none.

GOV-10.reason: An allow-list and priority cap enforced in code; the README's daily limit and audit log of blocked drafts do not exist.

MAL-20.reason: The widget is still a keyword bot; the model only drafts rules.

AIR-01.reason: One provider endpoint; the model is chosen by environment variable.

AIR-06.reason: No evaluation runs before a prompt or model change; the prompt-check job only checks the file exists and has a placeholder.

EXP-04.reason: Unanswered questions are recorded and grouped in queryable form; no themes outside the domain.

DEL-01.reason: Intake is a form; the model does not summarise or structure requests.

DEL-04.reason: The model drafts rule changes on request; a lead finishes them.

LRN-05.reason: Grouping is rule-based SQL; rule-based grouping counts as 0 for the AI reading.

LRN-06.reason: The model drafts proposals for one area, citing the failed questions.

LRN-07.reason: The model drafts candidate changes from experience on request.

LRN-08.reason: Automated checks on AI-made changes; no baseline evaluation.

GOV-10.reason: An allow-list in code for the one AI path; no blast-radius or rate limit.

MAL-20.reason: No model-backed conversation; the widget matches keywords.

main_count.reason: Routing rules (164) and answers (139) are nearly all requests.

kinds.label: routing rules
kinds.reason: The AI drafts rules and a lead completes and publishes them: Drafted.

kinds.label: answers
kinds.reason: Leads change answers with checks, history and undo; the AI does not draft answers.

kinds.label: greeting and opening hours
kinds.reason: Self-serve but with no undo, so reach 0.

kinds.label: queues
kinds.reason: A new queue is a config file edit and a release.

request.reason: AI lane (DEL-04 2), structured intake (DEL-01 2), checks (DEL-05 2) and every architecture criterion at 1 or more; L3 fails on rollback and controls.

fix.reason: Grouped failures (LRN-05 2) and drafted proposals (LRN-06 2) on top of the L1 conditions.

expansion.reason: DEL-04 2 gives a build path; no adjacent-capability proposals (EXP-05) for L2.
